newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to watch forex market carefully - MOF minister.
newsitem.headline: Japan to watch forex market carefully - MOF minister.

text.p: Japan will keep careful watch over moves in the foreign exchange market, newly appointed Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday.
Mitsuzuka said: "Movements in the foreign exchange market are those of a free market and they reflect overall economic conditions. We will carefully watch over these (movements)."
Asked about Tokyo's stock market, he said its movements were determined "by buying and selling."
"All we can do is carefully watch over it objectively," he said.
Tokyo stock prices dropped sharply on Thursday, with the key 225-share Nikkei average falling 1.05 percent to finish at 20,771.11.

Concerning the planned hike in the consumption tax, Mitsuzuka said the government will implement it as scheduled on April 1. The tax is due to be raised to five percent from the current three percent.

Regarding whether the government would continue the special cuts in income taxes it had implemented as an economic stimulus measure, Mitsuzuka said the government would make a decision on this upon looking at economic movements.
He said that if a supplementary budget with economic stimulus measures for 1996/97 was to be considered, it must take into account the economic and the nation's tight finances.
At the same time, the drafting of an extra budget must not delay the main state budget for next fiscal year, which starts on April 1, Mitsuzuka said.

The debt incurred by Japan's former state-owned railway -- now privatised as the Japan Railway group of companies -- must be dealt with because if left as is, it would inevitably increase, he said without elaborating.

Mitsuzuka said he was open to realistic suggestions by his ministry's officials about reforming the Finance Ministry. He also said he hoped to submit a bill to the next regular session of parliament, which starts in January, on such reforms.
